content.value_statement: Large repositories are hard to understand quickly. This skill maps structure, imports, entry points, and module boundaries for focused analysis.
actual_capabilities: Generates a filtered repository file tree that excludes common build and cache directories.
Parses Python imports with the standard AST parser.
Extracts JavaScript and TypeScript imports with pattern matching.
Builds a dependency graph with files, internal links, and external packages.
Identifies common Python and Node entry points.
Lists key files for types, execution, tools, agents, and configuration.
limitations: Dependency parsing is limited to Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, and TSX files.
Dynamic imports and unusual module loading patterns may be missed.
The script does not validate package versions or dependency health.
Generated output may include a local repository path unless the script is changed.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Create a quick structure map before reading many files manually.

use_cases.title: Prepare an architecture review
use_cases.description: Identify entry points, module boundaries, and key files before deeper design analysis.

use_cases.title: Scope an AI-assisted refactor
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a compact map before planning changes.

prompt_templates.title: Map a repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use codebase-mapping on this repository. Summarize the file tree, dependency graph, entry points, and key files in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Find entry points
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the codebase mapping workflow and focus on likely startup files, command-line entry points, and framework entry files.

prompt_templates.title: Explain module boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this repository and describe the main modules, their responsibilities, and important internal dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a refactor from the map
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the generated codebase map to identify risky dependency clusters, stable module boundaries, and files to inspect before refactoring.

output_examples.input: Map a Python web service before adding a feature.
output: Structure summary with source packages, configuration files, and test areas.
Entry point notes for the application server and command-line tasks.
Key files to inspect before changing request handling.

output_examples.input: Analyze a TypeScript package for onboarding.
output: Dependency overview showing internal modules and external packages.
Likely package entry points and exported surfaces.
Suggested reading order for a new contributor.

output_examples.input: Prepare for an architecture review of an agent project.
output: Map of agent, execution, tool, type, and configuration files.
Module boundary notes for review preparation.
Areas that need manual inspection because dynamic imports may be missed.

best_practices: Run the mapper on a clean local checkout so generated structure matches the current code.
Review excluded directories before using it on monorepos with custom build folders.
Use the generated map as a starting point, then inspect important files manually.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the dependency graph as complete when the project uses dynamic imports.
Do not share generated reports without checking for local paths or sensitive module names.
Do not use the map as a substitute for tests, runtime tracing, or design review.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code from the target repository?
faq.answer: No. The script reads files and parses imports. It does not run application code.

faq.question: Which languages does dependency mapping support?
faq.answer: It supports Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, and TSX dependency extraction.

faq.question: Can it map monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes, but very large monorepos may need custom exclusions and manual follow-up.

faq.question: Does it find every dependency?
faq.answer: No. Dynamic imports, generated code, and unusual loaders may require manual review.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use the output?
faq.answer: Yes. The map can give Claude Code, Codex, and Claude useful context before edits.

faq.question: Is the generated report safe to share?
faq.answer: Review it first. It may include local paths, file names, and module names from the repository.
